updates.source_content:
Supports Python 3.9 – Python 3.14

New Features
------------------------------
* New pragma `hy`.

Misc. Improvements
------------------------------
* Added compatibility with setuptools 80.3.0.

Bug Fixes
------------------------------
* Fixed a crash from using an empty string in a `(. …)` expression.
* `(except [[]] …)` now catches no exceptions, rather than being treated like `(except [] …)`, which catches all exceptions.
* `(except [e []] …)` is now translated to Python correctly by `hy2py`.
* Fixed a bug where logical ops starting with a `(setv …)` expression failed to compile.
* A complex `imag` argument to `hy.models.Complex` is no longer allowed.

# awesome-selfhosted 1.0.0

Visit the improved version of the Awesome-Selfhosted list at **https://awesome-selfhosted.net/**

_Awesome-Selfhosted is a list of [Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_software) Software [network services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_service) and [web applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application) which can be hosted on your own server(s). Self-hosting is the practice of hosting and managing applications on your own server(s) instead of consuming from [SaaSS](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/who-does-that-server-really-serve.html) providers._

The website at [awesome-selfhosted.net](https://awesome-selfhosted.net/) is now the recommended way to browse the list. It features improved search, categorization, layout, more detailed information, and should generally provide a better browsing experience. The old, familiar [markdown version](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted) of the list will keep receiving automated updates for the foreseeable future. 

You are encouraged to use, modify, improve and redistribute the list under the terms [of the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). Raw data, tools used to build markdown and HTML versions, issues and pull requests are now available under the [awesome-selfhosted-data repository](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted-data). You can find information on how to contribute to the project [here](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted-data/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md). 

Thanks to more than [1200 contributors](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted/graphs/contributors) for keeping this project going since 2015.

updates.source_content:
- Update tests for Claude Sonnet 4.5

Refs #54

Refs https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/pull/55#issuecomment-3535270497

- Use new structured output mechanism for Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.1 (#55)

* Add support for native structured outputs API

Implements native structured outputs for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.1
using the output_format parameter with the structured-outputs-2025-11-13
beta header. Uses transform_schema() from the Anthropic SDK to ensure
schema compliance.

For models that support structured outputs, uses the new API mechanism
instead of the tools workaround. Older models continue to use the
existing tools-based approach for backward compatibility.

Streaming is supported via create(stream=True) for structured outputs,
as the stream() helper method expects a Pydantic type rather than a dict.
Response JSON is properly reconstructed from streaming chunks.

Requires anthropic>=0.73.0.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Refs #54

* Refactor structured outputs to use stream() with dynamic Pydantic models

Instead of using create(stream=True) workaround, dynamically convert JSON
schemas to Pydantic models using create_model(). This allows using the
cleaner stream() helper method which expects a Pydantic type.

The _json_schema_to_pydantic() helper maps JSON schema types to Python
types and creates a dynamic BaseModel that can be passed to stream().

Suppresses harmless Pydantic serialization warnings that occur when
model_dump() is called on ParsedBetaMessage containing dynamic models.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Refs #54

* Use json-schema-to-pydantic library for schema conversion

Replaces custom _json_schema_to_pydantic implementation with the
json-schema-to-pydantic library which provides more robust handling
of JSON Schema features including complex types, references, and
validation constraints.

Reduces code by 38 lines and provides better schema support.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Refs #54

* Refactor structured outputs to use constructor parameter

Instead of checking claude_model_id against STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MODELS
set at runtime, add use_structured_outputs boolean parameter to model
constructor and set it during registration.

This makes the decision about structured outputs support a registration-
time configuration rather than a runtime check, which is cleaner and
more explicit.

Removes the STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MODELS set entirely as it's no longer
needed.

Refs #54

* Extract warning suppression into helper method

Refactors inline warning suppression code into a dedicated
_model_dump_suppress_warnings() helper method with clear documentation
explaining why the suppression is necessary.

When using dynamically created Pydantic models with the SDK's stream()
helper, the returned ParsedBetaMessage has strict type annotations that
don't match our dynamic models, causing harmless serialization warnings.
The helper method suppresses these warnings while still producing correct
output.

Refs #54

* Ditch pointless wrapper method

updates.title: v0.2.0
updates.source_content:
This release includes a major update on the `TreeQuest` interface (#14).

## Ask-Tell Interface
We added ask-tell interface, where users run `ask` or `ask_batch` to get the parent state and action of the next node to expand in the search tree. Using the returned `Trial` object, users run `generate_fn` to calculate the score and state of the expanded node, and update the search tree with `tell` interface. 

This new interface enables us to

1. Perform multiple AB-MCTS sampling steps in parallel by `ask_batch`.
2. Run multiple generation processes in parallel and run `tell` once an evaluation process finishes.

so that now both TreeQuest itself and users can leverage more cpu resource to speed up the tree search.

For the performance for different batch sizes, please see `docs/PROFILING.md`.

updates.title: Updates in main (5 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление представляет новый пакет `lem-bookmark`. Оно также значительно повышает надежность сборок Nix, исправляя проблемы с получением хеша git и устраняя две критические ошибки сборки Lem через Nix flakes на Linux. В частности, были решены проблемы с компиляцией библиотеки `async-process` и управлением зависимостью `lem-extension-manager` от Quicklisp в изолированных средах, что обеспечивает успешные сборки Nix без влияния на традиционные методы.
updates.source_content:
- Merge pull request #2006 from mychris/feature/bookmark-extension

Adds a new bookmark package.

- Fix git hash retrieval during Nix builds

- Skip git operations when :nix-build feature is set
- Run git command in repository root instead of .git/ directory
- Add error handling to prevent build failures when git command fails

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

- tweak colors

- bookmark: Renames the package from bookmark to lem-bookmark.

- Fix Nix build failures in flake.nix (#2007)

This commit resolves two build failures when building Lem via Nix flakes:

1. async-process library build error: The Makefile referenced a Windows-specific
   source file (async-process_windows.c) that doesn't exist on Linux, causing
   make to fail. Added sed command to remove Windows source references and
   properly build and copy the shared library.

2. lem-extension-manager QL-DIST dependency: The extension manager depends on
   Quicklisp's QL-DIST package which is unavailable in Nix's sandboxed build
   environment. Introduced a :nix-build feature flag that conditionally excludes
   lem-extension-manager during Nix builds while preserving it for standard builds.

These changes enable successful Nix flake builds on Linux without affecting
traditional build methods (Roswell, qlot, manual builds).

updates.title: Updates in main (1 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Рефакторинг vcpu нарушил поддержку gdb, приводя к взаимоблокировке из-за неверного порядка создания потока и двойной блокировки VMM. Данное исправление устраняет обе проблемы, обеспечивая корректную работу поддержки gdb. Дополнительно добавлено больше логирования для ошибок GDB, что поможет при отладке.
updates.source_content:
- fix(gdb): remove wrong ordering and double locking

With the vcpu refactoring gdb support got broken. While we have a test
to verify it builds, we still don't have one to verify it works.
In particular, the gdb thread was created too early, and the vmm was
locked twice leading to a deadlock.

This change fixes both issues and adds a little bit more logging for the
errors in GDB which were helpful to debug the issue.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

updates.title: Updates in main (6 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление представляет устройство VMClock для гостевых систем x86_64, включая включение его Kconfig для Linux 6.1, добавление начальной реализации, интеграционных тестов и привязок Rust ABI на основе Linux 6.13. Хотя устройство в настоящее время выделяет память и поддерживает маркеры прерываний, оно пока не предоставляет часы хоста и не поддерживает живую миграцию. Одновременно упрощена конструкция устройства ACPI VMGenID.
updates.source_content:
- guest-kernels: add VMClock config for 6.1

5.10 already had the VMClock Kconfig enabled, whereas 6.1 didn't. Patch
the 6.1 to add the missing Kconfig option

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

- vmclock: add integration tests

Add tests that validate that VMClock device as exposed inside the guest
under /dev/vmclock0 works as expected. This includes a small C program
that knows how to open and read values from /dev/vmclock0.

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

- vmclock: add support for VMclock device for x86_64

Implement the VMClock device on x86_64 platforms. At the moment, we just
allocate the memory region in the guest address space for exposing the
device. We don't expose any clock from the host and since we don't
support live migration, the device won't do anything at the moment, but
we should still be able to see a `/dev/vmclock` inside the guest.

We do support the `disruption_marker` field which notifies the guest to
adjust clocks due to a time shifting event.

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

- vmclock: add vmclock ABI Rust bindings

Add bindings for vmclock ABI from Linux 6.13, also add the logic in
tools/bindgen.sh to automate the process.

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

- acpi: simplify the construction of VMGenID device

Decouple creation of VMGenID device with writing the generation ID in
guest memory. This way we can avoid keeping an `Option<VmGenId>` inside
the ACPI device manager. We can always create it and only write the
generation ID in guest memory once we are ready to activate the device
(when we have a functioning guest memory object).

Also, remove a few of the error types and fail in-place instead of
propagating errors all the way up.

On the Aarch64, we need to recreate the expected dtb files because
default microVMs always create entries for the VMGenID device.

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

- bindgen: upgrade to linux 6.13 headers

vmclock is added in Linux 6.13. Upgrade the version we are using to
create Rust bindings from to this version so we can get vmclock ABI
definitions.

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Эта серия изменений в основном направлена на улучшение обработки MSR (Model-Specific Register) на архитектуре x86_64 для гостевых операционных систем. Критическое исправление затрагивает MSR IA32_MTRRdefType, позволяя гостям правильно устанавливать типы памяти для таких областей, как pmem, в write-back, устраняя предыдущие проблемы с производительностью, когда они помечались как uncached-minus. Кроме того, IA32_PAT_MSR добавлен в список исключений, что дает гостям больше контроля над атрибутами страниц, а значения MTRR MSR теперь автоматически генерируются для улучшения удобства обслуживания.
updates.source_content:
- chore: add note to CHANGELOG

Add note about IA32_MTRRdefType MSR to CHANGELOG.

Signed-off-by: Egor Lazarchuk <yegorlz@amazon.co.uk>

- chore(x86_64): add IA32_PAT_MSR to the exception list

IA32_PAT_MSR can be modified by the guest to change
page attributes for memory regions.

Signed-off-by: Egor Lazarchuk <yegorlz@amazon.co.uk>

- refactor(x86_64): use generated MSR values instead of hand coded ones

Replace hand coded MTRR MSRs with auto generated ones.

Signed-off-by: Egor Lazarchuk <yegorlz@amazon.co.uk>

- fix(x86_64): specify IA32_MTRRdefType MSR on boot

The IA32_MTRRdefType MSR describes the default memory type
used for physical addresses which are outside of any configured
memory ranges, as well as whether MTRRs and fixed ranges
are enabled.

Without enabling this MSR, guest kernel is not able to change
memory types for memory ranges outside main memory. This was
causing pmem region to be marked as `uncached-minus` which
instructed the cpu to skip all caches (L1, L2, L3) when
reading/writing to that memory region.

To fix this set IA32_MTRRdefType set to 0x806:
- bit 11 enables MTRR
- bits 0..7 specify the memory type used by default
  - value 6 represents `write-back` type

Now guest can correctly set pmem memory region to
`write-back` memory type.

Signed-off-by: Egor Lazarchuk <yegorlz@amazon.co.uk>

updates.title: Updates in main (2 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Добавлен новый скрипт `ab_plot.py` для визуализации данных о производительности, поддерживающий сравнение различных входов, хостов и тестов, с возможностью вывода в PDF и HTML. Для этого потребовалось добавить библиотеки `numpy`, `pandas` и `seaborn`, а также обновить версию Python. Обновление версии Python повлекло за собой изменение способа установки Poetry и необходимость ручной установки `python3-venv`.
updates.source_content:
- feat: add numpy, pandas and seaborn to poentry.toml

These libraries are needed for the ab_plot.py.
At the same time update `python` version defined in the
`pyproject.toml`. This is required because for some reason
poetry errors when pooling dependencies saying the python
version is too old. Updating the python version caused
other problems with poetry installation with `pip3 install`.
Because of this, change the way poetry is insatlled by
pooling it directly from a website. Additionally the change
broke somehow `virtualenv`, so just install `python3-venv` manually.

Signed-off-by: Egor Lazarchuk <yegorlz@amazon.co.uk>

- feat: add ab_plot.py script

Add a script to create visualizations of performance data.
- works for both single and multiple inputs
- allows comparison of different hosts
- allows comparison of multiple tests
- can generate pdf and html outputs

Signed-off-by: Egor Lazarchuk <yegorlz@amazon.co.uk>

updates.title: Updates in main (48 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Внедрено и полностью реализовано устройство virtio-mem, обеспечивающее возможности горячего подключения памяти. Это включает в себя определение новых API (GET, PUT, PATCH), добавление статического и динамического выделения горячо подключаемой памяти с управлением слотами KVM, а также защиту отключаемых областей с помощью mprotect. Функция тщательно задокументирована, поддерживается обширными интеграционными тестами и тестами производительности, а также содержит различные исправления и улучшения для обеспечения стабильности и корректности.
updates.source_content:
- chore(changelog): add entry for virtio-mem hotplugging

Add an entry for memory hotplugging support.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(tests/virtio-mem): poll every 5ms in performance tests

Increase granularity of total time measurement from 100ms to 5ms as the
fastest hotplug is around 30ms.

We need to poll the GET API to monitor when plugged_memory_mib is equal
to requested_memory_mib.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- doc: add link from README to virtio-pmem and -mem docs

Add the two new features in the "Features and Compatibilities" section
of the main README.md.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- doc(virtio-mem): add memory hotplug documentation

This adds documentation for the new memory hotplug feature.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(memory): validate memory state in snapshot_state_sanity_check

Add validation about the memory regions stored in the memory state:
 - we need at least 1 region
 - we need at least 1 DRAM region
 - all DRAM regions need to have a single plugged slot

This issue was caught by the fuzzer snapshot harness.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(tests/virtio-mem): increase base VM memory size to hotplug 16GB

The previously set 256MB were not enough for hotplugging 16GB of memory.
This is because the kernel needs 64B for every 4kB page, meaning 262MB
for 16GB.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(tests/virtio-mem): bump fillmem timeout to 30s

Sometimes on m6a the uffd test fails to write 1.2GB within 10s. Bump the
timeout to 30s.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(mmio/persist): do not unwrap error if VirtioMem restore fails

Return the error up the stack instead of unwrapping it.

Note that on PCI this error is unwrapped for every device so there's no
change there.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix: store bitvec as Vec<bool> to prevent fuzzer crashes

When the fuzzer generates an invalid bitvec state, the serde code
crashes with an assertion error.
To avoid these crashes, just store it as a plain Vec<bool> as we don't
expect these vecs to be too big (for a 10GB hotpluggable area with 2MiB
blocks it would require 5kB for the Vec<bool> compared to 640B with
BitVec).

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): test incremental snapshots

Add a test that verifies that incremental snapshots work as expected.
Each generation will plug more memory and verify that the contents in
memory from previous generations are persisted.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): test multiple snapshot methods

Extend the tests to also check that everything works with diff snapshots
(dirty page tracking and mincore).

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor: remove clone_vm and extend build_from_snapshot to accept uffd

These two functions were doing a similar thing. Let's extend the
build_from_snapshot to support uffd and drop the newly introduced
clone_vm.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): mprotect unplugged memory ranges

This prevents the device emulation to be tricked into accessing
unplugged memory ranges. If a malicious driver tries to do so, the VMM
will crash with a memory error.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- chore(bk): add memory-hotplug pipeline definition to perf tests

Add the memory hotplug tests to buildkite.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): add performance test

Add a performance test that measures the latency to hot(un)plug
different amounts of memory.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): implement dynamic slots

Dynamically plug/unplug KVM slots when any/all of the blocks are
plugged/unplugged.

This prevents the guest from accessing unplugged memory.
However, this doesn't yet prevent the device emulation from accessing
the slots.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(mem): introduce KVM slots per GuestMemoryRegion

A single GuestMemoryRegion can be split into multiple KVM slots. This is
used for Hotplug type regions where we can dynamically remove access to
the region from the guest.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor(mincore): pass addr and len to mincore_bitmap

In preparation to adding support for multiple memory slots, refactor the
mincore_bitmap function to accept a pointer and length rather than an
entire memory region object.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor: define a set_user_memory_region function in Vm

To avoid boilerplate code in multiple places, let's just define it once
and use it everywhere.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor: allow reserving multiple kvm slots at once

Add a slot_cnt parameter to next_kvm_slot. This will be used to allocate
multiple slots for a slotted hotpluggable region.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): add rust integration tests

These tests add unit test coverage to the builder.rs and vm.rs files
which where previously untested in the memory hotplug case.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- chore(test/virtio-mem): move tests under performance

Since these tests need to be run on an ag=1 host, move them under the
"performance" folder.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): add functional integration tests for device

Add integration tests for the new device:
 - check that the device is detected
 - check that hotplugging and unplugging works
 - check that memory can be used after hotplugging
 - check that memory is freed on hotunplug
 - check different config combinations
 - check different uvm types
 - check that contents are preserved across snapshot-restore

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor(test/balloon): move logic to get guest avail mem to framework

Move the logic to get the MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo inside the
guest to a new guest_stats module in the test framework. This provides a
new class MeminfoGuest that can be used to retrieve this information
(and more!).

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(test/balloon): include HugePages in RSS measurements

This moves the logic to measure RSS to framework.utils and adds a logic
to also include huge pages in the measurement.

Furthermore, this also adds caching for the firecracker_pid, as well as
a new property to get the corresponding psutil.Process.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(examples/uffd): unregister range on UFFD Remove event

If the handler receives a UFFD remove event, it currently stores the PFN
and will reply with a zero page whenever it receives a pagefault event
for that page.
This works well with 4k pages, but zeropage is not supported on
hugepages. In order to support hugepages, let's just unregister from
UFFD whenever we get a remove event. By doing so, the handler won't
receive a notification for the removed page, and the VM will get a new
zero page from the kernel.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(metrics): add virtio-mem device metrics to validation

Add the virtio-mem device metrics to the integ test validation.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): add unit tests for virtio queue request handling

Adds unit tests using VirtioTestHelper to verify correct functioning of
the new device.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): implement virtio requests

This commit adds block state management and implements the virtio
requests for the virtio-mem device.

Block state is tracked using a BitVec, each bit representing a single
block.

Plug/Unplug requests are validated before being executed to verify the
range is valid (aligned and within range), and that all blocks in range
are unplugged/plugged, as per the virtio spec.

UplugAll is the only request where usable_region_size can be lowered.

This commit is missing the dynamic KVM slot management which will be
added later.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): add virtio request parsing and dummy response

Parse virtio requests over the queue and always ack them. Following
commits will add the state management inside the device.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): add API tests for PATCH

Test that the new PATCH API behaves as expected.
Also updates expected metrics and fixes memory monitor to account for
hotplugging.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- doc(virtio-mem): document PATCH API in swagger and docs

Add entry for the patch API in Swagger and in the docs.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): wire PATCH support

Wire up PATCH requests with the virtio-mem device.
All the validation is performed in the device, but the actual operation
is not yet implemented.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): add static allocation of hotpluggable memory

Allocate the memory that will be used for hotplugging. Initially, this
memory will be registered with KVM, but that will change later when we
add dynamic slot support.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): add metrics for virtio-mem device

Wire support for virtio-mem metrics, adding a few basic metrics: queue
events, queue event fails, activation fails.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): implement snapshot/restore

Implements basic snapshot/restore functionality for the dummy virtio-mem
device.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor(virtio-mem): remove type annotation

This type annotation is redoundant, so we can remove it.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor(virtio-mem): use u64_to_usize instead of try_into+unwrap

It's better to be explicit on the conversion we're doing as u64 to usize
is always safe in our platforms.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- fix(test/virtio-mem): ensure RuntimeError is raised with matching reason

We should match the exact reason for the RuntimeError to ensure we're
failing for what we're expecting.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- refactor(virtio-mem): define constants as MiB

Avoid multiple conversions back and forth from MiB to bytes by just
storing as MiB.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- chore(doc): update documentation for new API

Add new API to swagger and device-api.md

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- feat(virtio-mem): add GET API

Add support for GET /hotplug/memory that returns the current status of
the virtio-mem device.

This API can only be called after boot.

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

- test(virtio-mem): add integ test to verify device is detected

Check that the driver correctly detects the virtio-mem device, with the

Add a dummy virtio-mem device that is detected by the guest driver.

updates.title: Updates in main (13 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление представляет две новые функции управления памятью для устройства virtio-balloon Firecracker: подсказку свободных страниц (free page hinting) и отчетность свободных страниц (free page reporting). Эти механизмы позволяют гостевой ОС информировать хост о неиспользуемых страницах памяти, что позволяет хосту более эффективно высвобождать их, включая огромные страницы. Подсказка страниц предлагает отчетность по запросу с управлением через API, тогда как отчетность страниц непрерывно уведомляет хост для снижения RSS виртуальной машины.
updates.source_content:
- changelog: Added free page hinting and reporting

Update changelog to include free page hinting and reporting.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- docs: Add free page hinting documentation

Update docs to include details about the new free page hinting feature
in firecracker.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- docs: Add free page reporting documentation

Update the balloon documentation to include a section about free page
reporting.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- docs: Update documentation for huge pages and balloon

Update docs to reflect that now huge pages can be used alongside the
traditional balloon device. However, note the caveat that memory may not
be reclaimed from the guest.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- virtio-balloon: Drop huge page restriction

While the traditional balloon device would not be able to reclaim memory
when back by huge pages, it could still technically be used to to
restrict memory usage in the guest.

With the addition of hinting and reporting, they report ranges in bigger
sizes (4mb by default). Because of this, it is possible for the host
reclaim huge pages backing the guest.

Updates the performance tests for the balloon when back by huge pages,
added varients to the size reduction tests to ensure hinting and
reporting can reduce the RSS of the guest.

Move the inflation test to performance to ensure it runs sequentially in
CI otherwise the host can be exhausted of huge pages.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- test: Add unit tests for hint/reporting

Add unit tests for free page hinting and reporting. Asserting the
features are enabled correctly. Testing the config space updates
triggered by hinting are being set as expected.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- test: Add integration tests for hinting/reporting

Add integration tests for free page hinting and reporting, both
functional and performance tests.

New functional tests to ensure that hinting and reporting are reducing
the RSS as expected in the guest. Updated reduce RSS test to touch
memory to reduce the chance of flakiness.

New performance tests for the balloon device. First being a test to
track the CPU overhead of hinting and reporting. Second being a test to
measure the faulting latency while reporting is running in the guest.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- test: Add oneshot mode to fast page fault helper

Add option for fast_page_fault_helper to run in a oneshot mode, that
doesn't require the signal to be triggered before measuring the fault
latency.

This makes it possible to test fault latency on non-snapshotted vms as
only the first fault is measured.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- test: Add API hinting endpoints

Adding new resources to the http api to enable testing of the hinting
functionality.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- virtio-balloon: Add metrics for hinting/reporting

Add metrics to track free page hinting and reporting. For both devices
track the number of ranges reported, the number of errors encountered
while freeing and the total amount of memory freed.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- virtio-balloon: Add api for free page hinting

Adding API endpoints to manage free page hinting . With
three different endpoint: Start - To begin a new run for free page
hinting, Status - To track the state of the hinting run, Stop - To stop
the hinting run and allow the guest to reclaim the pages reported.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- virtio-balloon: Add free page hinting

Free page hinting is a mechanism which allows the guest driver to report
ranges of pages to the host device. A "hinting" run is triggered by the
device by issuing a new command id in the config space, after the update
to the id the device will hint ranges to the host which are unused. Once
the driver has exhausted all free ranges it notifies the device the run
has completed. The device can then issue another command allowing the
guest to reclaim these pages.

Adding support for hinting the firecracker balloon device, we offer
three points to manage the device; first to start a run, second to
monitor the status and a final to issue the command to allow the guest
to reclaim pages.

To note, there is a potential condition in the linux driver which would
allow a range to be reclaimed in an oom scenario before we remove the
range.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

- virtio-balloon: Add free page reporting

Free page reporting is a mechanism in which the guest will notify the
host of pages which are not currently in use. This feature can only be
configured on boot and will continue to report continuously.

With free page reporting firecracker will `MADV_DONTNEED` on the ranges
reported. This allows the host to free up memory and reduce the RSS of
the VM. With UFFD this is sent as the `UFFD_EVENT_REMOVE` after the call
with `MADV_DONTNEED`.

Signed-off-by: Jack Thomson <jackabt@amazon.com>

updates.summary_ru: Было реализовано два исправления. Одно устранило ошибку компиляции в `fast_page_fault_helper`, где `getopt_long` не хватало ожидаемых аргументов. Второе исправление отключило функцию `bindgen` в `aws-lc-rs`, поскольку предварительно собранные привязки сделали ее избыточной, а ее использование добавляло минуту к времени сборки, тем самым значительно ускоряя компиляцию.
updates.source_content:
- fix(rootfs): fix fast_page_fault_helper compilation

There was a compilation error in the file where getopt_long expects argc
and argv arguments of main() but these weren't declared. Maybe a rebase
gone bad(?)

Signed-off-by: Babis Chalios <bchalios@amazon.es>

- fix(build): disable bindgen feature of aws-lc-rs

Since 1.15 it's no longer necessary to run bindgen on every build since
bindings are now prebuilt and distributed for common platforms [1].
From 1.15, this bindgen is taking even longer, increasing our
compilation times by 1 minute!

Remove the now unnecessary feature to speed up builds.

[1]: https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs/pull/896

Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

updates.title: Updates in master (2 commits)
updates.summary_ru: `Gptel` был обновлен для улучшения обработки наложений при подтверждении вызовов инструментов, что предотвращает проблемы при изменении активного буфера Emacs языковой моделью. Также исправлена логика парсинга потоковых ответов, благодаря чему пустые фрагменты внутри блоков рассуждений теперь корректно интерпретируются как часть рассуждений. Это устраняет ошибки в разметке и категоризации текста, которые ранее возникали при некорректной обработке пустых строк.
updates.source_content:
- gptel: Fix overlay handling in tool call confirmation cleanup

* gptel.el (gptel--accept-tool-calls, gptel--reject-tool-calls):
When cleaning up the tool call confirmation overlays, set the
buffer to the overlay buffer.  Otherwise this creates issues when
the tool call changes the active Emacs buffer, which happpens
often when an LLM is controlling Emacs.

- gptel-request: Fix blank response check inside reasoning block

* gptel-request.el (gptel-curl--stream-filter): Update reasoning
block parsing logic when streaming.  Now:
1. blank response chunks before reasoning blocks are ignored by
the reasoning parser.  (Same as before)
2. blank response chunks inside a reasoning block are captured as
reasoning text by the parser. (New behavior)

Without this, reasoning text consisting of blank strings is
categorized as a response, causing the reasoning block demarcation
to fail and additional "#+begin_reasoning" (or equivalent markup)
to be inserted by gptel's default streaming callback.

updates.title: Updates in master (1 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Функция `gptel-context-remove-all` была обновлена в файле `gptel-context.el`. Это изменение потребовалось из-за модификации спецификации `gptel-context`. Теперь области буфера указываются в plist с ключом `:overlays`, а не как список оверлеев, что потребовало соответствующего обновления функции.
updates.source_content:
- gptel-context: Fix overlay handling in gptel-context-remove-all

* gptel-context.el (gptel-context-remove-all): After the
`gptel-context' spec change, buffer regions in the context are
specified in a plist with the :overlays key and not a list of
overlays.  Update `gptel-context-remove-all' to handle
this. (#1142)

Функция `gptel-track-media`, которая контролирует отправку медиафайлов, теперь отделена от файлов, явно добавленных в контекст с помощью `gptel-add-file`. `gptel-track-media` теперь относится исключительно к буферам чата, в то время как файлы, добавленные напрямую через `gptel-add-file`, всегда будут отправляться.

* gptel-request.el (gptel--realize-query): Decouple
`gptel-track-media' behavior from media files added to the context
via `gptel-add-file'.  `gptel-track-media' is intended to only be
relevant to chat buffers, like `gptel-track-response'.  Media
files added explicitly to the context should always be sent.

updates.title: Updates in master (2 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление вводит константу `gptel-version` для улучшения обратной совместимости. Однако основное изменение заключается в переработке способа оценки системных сообщений в `gptel-request`: теперь они обрабатываются непосредственно в буфере запроса, что гарантирует оценку функций в текущей среде пользователя. Кроме того, было реализовано исправление, которое сохраняет строковые системные подсказки как строки до окончательной реализации запроса, решая проблемы с пресетами.
updates.source_content:
- gptel: Add version constant for runtime checks

* gptel.el (gptel-version): Add constant for runtime checks of
gptel's version, to help with backward compatibility in features
that use gptel.

- gptel-request: Evaluate system messages in request buffer

* gptel-request.el (gptel-request): Parse the system message,
evaluating function-valued system messages in the process, in the
request buffer instead of the temporary prompt buffer used to
construct the prompt.  (#1095, #1153)

This is necessary for correctness, since the system message
function is intended by the user to be evaluated in their current
environment.

The parsed system message (as returned by gptel--parse-directive)
is always a list, even when the original directive is a string.
This can cause issues when applying presets in the prompt that
modify the system message by appending to it.  To avoid this,
ensure that string-valued system prompts remain string-valued
until the query is finally realized in `gptel--realize-query'.

This latter fix is ugly, but the alternative is to make
`gptel--parse-directive' a polymorphic, sum-type function, which
appears to be uglier on the whole considering its many uses in
gptel's request pipeline and UI.

* NEWS (New features and UI changes): Mention bug fix.

updates.summary_ru: Недавние обновления включают оптимизацию Makefile за счет удаления неиспользуемых и неисправных хуков для Windows, что делает его предназначенным только для Linux/MacOS и упрощает поддержку. Были внесены улучшения в функциональность `drop_table()`, предусматривающие многофазное удаление, добавление транзакционного состояния и улучшение действий по накату каталога. Кроме того, было реализовано изменение протокола для публикации существующих версий, а также новая валидация для `table.md`.
updates.source_content:
- Changes to protocol to handle publishing existing version           (#938)

Adding validation for table.md to have at least one entry

- Streamline Makefile (#937)

No one seems to be using or maintaining the Windows hooks in our
Makefile, and they're already broken in several places. This backs them
out so that the Makefile is once again Linux/MacOS only, which
streamlines the Makefile and makes it easier to maintain. If Windows
support becomes important again we'll need to redo it anyway.

(This won't affect any customers using Pixeltable on Windows.)

- Multi-phase drop_table() (#932)

In order to accommodate multi-phase drop:
- adds more transactional state to TableMd
- adds roll-forward action to Catalog
- changes initialization of StoreBase to avoid references to a view's
base (so that the sa_table of a StoreView can be initialized w/o the
base table still being present)

Оно также улучшает обработку ошибок благодаря усовершенствованному обнаружению повторяемых ошибок в `RequestRateScheduler` для исключений TwelveLabs. updates.source_content:
- Rename `DataFrame` to `Query` and `DataFrameResultSet` to `ResultSet` (#902)

I tried to be as thorough as I could, renaming local variables and doc
references in addition to classes.

It wasn't entirely trivial, since `df` can also (and often does) mean
"Pandas DataFrame", and also appears as a substring of `udf`, `pdf`, and
`soundfile`. But I did my best to rename carefully.

With this change, we can detect retry-after inside a TwelveLabs
exception

- Various Mintlify rendering improvements
- Cleaner build process

Mostly a copy of the fix in #840 but with Tigris instead of B2. I think
you may need to create a bucket in Tigris with test fixtures. If this is
the case I am more than happy to help!

Signed-off-by: Xe Iaso <xe@tigrisdata.com>

- Circularity detection in view creation with if_exists='replace' (#942)

Checks for a specific scenario in which:
- A view `my_view` is created
- A subview of `my_view` is created with the identical name `my_view`,
using if_exists='replace'

If this situation not detected, it leads to permanent catalog
corruption.

updates.summary_ru: Недавние обновления улучшают потоковую передачу прерываний, последовательно включая полное состояние с прерываниями в режиме `stream_mode="values"` и отображая прерывания как в чанках значений, так и в чанках обновлений для `stream_mode=["values", "updates"]`. Значительная переработка логики инъекции теперь гарантирует, что сигнатуры функций инструментов учитываются, позволяя внедрять критически важные аргументы, такие как `ToolRuntime` (который предоставляет ID вызова инструмента и состояние), даже если они явно не определены в `args_schema`. Это также обеспечивает повышение производительности и более чистый код.
updates.source_content:
- chore(sdk-py): Add more type checking. (#6479)

- fix: interrupt stream mode values (#6475)

This PR improves the consistency of interrupt streaming. 

- when streaming with stream_mode values, the stream chunk now contains
the entire state alongside the interrupt:

```python
class State(TypedDict):
    robot_input: str
# at this point in time robot_input is already set to  "beep boop i am a robot"
app.stream(..., stream_mode="values")
# before
{"__interrupt__": (Interrupt(value="interrupt",))}}
# after
{"robot_input": "beep boop i am a robot", "__interrupt__": (Interrupt(value="interrupt"))}
```

- when streaming with stream_mode=["values", "updates"], interrupts are
surfaced in both an update stream chunk and the value stream chunk, when
previously we keep interrupt in values only if we request values mode
only

```python
class State(TypedDict):
    robot_input: str
# at this point in time robot_input is already set to  "beep boop i am a robot"
app.stream(..., stream_mode=["values", "updates"])
# before (interrupt would only emit on update chunk, there would be no values chunk)
("updates", {"__interrupt__": (Interrupt(value="interrupt",))}})
# after
("updates", {"__interrupt__": (Interrupt(value="interrupt",))}})
("values", {"robot_input": "beep boop i am a robot", "__interrupt__": (Interrupt(value="interrupt"))})
```

For housekeeping: this PR improves on this revert:
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/6141

- release: langgraph-prebuilt 1.0.5 (#6473)

- fix: refactor injection logic to respect function signatures (#6468)

## overview

The main purpose of this is to respect tool signatures that request
injected args (like `ToolRuntime`) even when the explicitly specified
`args_schema` does not.

Ex in the following example, we should still inject `runtime` despite
its absence in `ArgsSchema`

```py
class ArgsSchema(BaseModel):
    some_arg: int = Field(...)

@tool(args_schema=ArgsSchema)
def my_tool(some_arg: int, runtime: ToolRuntime): ...
```

This is accompanied by
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/34051 which has tests
that pass w/ this change. This tests injection w/ `create_agent` (more
end to end than tests added in
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/33999.

This unblocks the injection of `ToolRuntime` into MCP tools which is
exciting bc that exposes tool call id and state, which we previously
were unable to do.

## other benefits

* Cleaner code structure w/ more helpful docs about injected args.
* Nice perf boost, we're no longer inspecting the annotations of a
tool's schema 3 different times to detect store, state, and runtime
injections.

## additional notes

1. I could see a world where we want more of this logic to reside on the
tools themselves, but tools don't now about LG specific injection types
(like `ToolRuntime`, hence having this logic here for now).
2. We could separately add validation for the case where something is
specified in `args_schema` and not in the function signature (probably
at the tool level though).

- [docs] rm `stagehand.page` from v3 snippets (#1271)

# why
- migration guide docs for v3 still included references to
`stagehand.page` which is not supported in v3
# what changed
- replaced with `stagehand.context.pages()[0]` and `await
stagehand.context.awaitActivePage()`

- fix: `setInputFiles()` not working on Browserbase (#1267)

# why
- file uploads were failing on Browserbase. this is because
`setInputFiles()` was not serializing the file payload
# what changed
changed business logic of `setInputFiles()` to: 
- call `normalizeInputFiles()`, which returns a serializable/base64
encoded file
- check if the browser is remote
- if remote, `assignFilesViaPayloadInjection()` is called, which then
calls `assignFilePayloadsToInputElement()` (browser-side JS) and
reconstructs the base64 back into a file, and directly assigns the
reconstructed files to the `input` element
- if not remote (local), then the files are written to temp dirs, and
those dirs are passed into `DOM.setInputFiles` (CDP command)
# test plan

- regression evals

updates.title: Updates in main (2 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Значительные оптимизации были внедрены для существенного улучшения производительности CI. Ключевые изменения включают распараллеливание задач оценки, что сокращает общее время CI примерно на 50% (с ~25 до ~12 минут). Также введено кэширование сборок для устранения избыточных процессов, улучшено управление зависимостями и добавлены интеллектуальные правила пропуска для определенных изменений кода. Кроме того, был добавлен минимальный контрактный тест для отслеживания структуры и экспортируемых элементов публичного API.
updates.source_content:
- Fm/stg 956 make ci faster (#1246)

# why

CI was slow due to sequential eval jobs, repeated builds, and
inefficient dependency management.

# what changed

Parallel Execution:
- Eval jobs now run in parallel instead of sequentially (regression →
all others in parallel)
  - Reduces total CI time from ~25 mins to ~12 mins

  Build Caching:
  - Build artifacts uploaded once and reused by all eval jobs
  - Eliminates 6 redundant builds (~2-3 min savings each)

  Smart Skipping:
  - skip-evals label: skip all evals
  - skip-regression-evals label: skip regression only
  - Auto-skip for docs-only changes (not on main)

  Dependency Optimization:
  - Use pnpm/action-setup@v4 with caching
  - Use --frozen-lockfile for deterministic installs
  - Remove unnecessary node_modules cleanup

  Test Parallelization:
  - Local tests: 2→3 workers (Browserbase), 2→4 workers (standard)
  - Better CI vs local environment detection

# test plan

 - Verify build artifacts upload/download correctly
  - Confirm eval jobs run in parallel after regression
  - Test skip-evals and skip-regression-evals labels work
  - Verify docs-only changes skip evals (except on main)
  - Measure CI time reduction (~50-60% expected)
  - Confirm no test flakiness from increased parallelization
  - All tests, lint, and build pass

Оно также устраняет критическую ошибку, из-за которой `waitForDomNetworkQuiet()` мог зависать на неопределенное время из-за некорректной обработки событий и управления таймаутами. Кроме того, были добавлены новые методы доступа для получения URL-адресов сессий и отладки Browserbase.
updates.source_content:
- add support for zod v4 (#1282)

Why 

Adds support for zod 4 while maintaining backwards compatibility with
zod 3

What changed 

- Introduced a zodCompat layer so Stagehand speaks both Zod v3 and v4
natively. Every place that used to import zod/v3, zod-to-json-schema, or
poke at schema internals now routes through the same helpers
(StagehandZodSchema, InferStagehandSchema, toJsonSchema, etc.). That
keeps existing apps on v3 working while letting us upgrade to the v4
ecosystem.
- Swapped all examples, eval tasks, tests, and LLM clients over to
standard zod imports, updated dependencies to accept 3.25.76 || 4.1.8,
and dropped zod-to-json-schema. Tool plumbing (Anthropic/Google CUA) and
custom clients now produce the right JSON Schema regardless of which Zod
flavor the user passes in.
- Tightened typings so structured LLM calls return { data, usage }
directly no more as casts throughout inference or the samples.

Manual testing
To make sure nothing regressed, I ran:
Custom OpenAI client example (schema conversion + structured output).
Standard extract (including URL injection path).
Google computer-use agent with a custom tool.
Anthropic computer-use agent with a custom tool.
All behaved as before

---------

- fix: `waitForDomNetworkQuiet()` can hang forever (#1284)

# why
- this PR fixes an issue where `waitForDomNetworkQuiet()` does not
resolve
- this issue is caused by 2-3 underlying issues:
- the first issue is that `frame.waitForLoadState()` was not listening
for the correct lifecycle events from CDP. instead of listening for
`DOMContentLoaded`, it was listening for `domcontentloaded`
- the second issue is that `frame.waitForLoadState()` did not accept a
timeout parameter
- the third issue is that `waitForDomNetworkQuiet()` did not include the
call to `frame.waitForLoadState()` as part of the total time that it
waits for
# what changed
- added string normalization of incoming lifecycle events from CDP in
`frame.waitForLoadState()` (fixes the first issue)
- added a timeout parameter to `frame.waitForLoadState()`
- within `waitForDomNetworkQuiet()`, I included the call to
`frame.waitForLoadState()` as part of the total time that it waits for
# test plan
- existing unit tests & regression evals should be ok

- add BB session URL & debug URL accessors (#1281)

# why
currently, stagehand just logs the BB session URL and debug URL inline
without storing this info on the stagehand object but we want getters
for these.

If env = browserbase, we return the urls, if it's local we return an
empty string currently as per the ticket. It seemed to me like returning
undefined if env = local might be better DX, but i'll double check w/
sean.

# what changed
Added getters and a small `resetBrowserbaseSessionMetadata()` helper.

# test plan
Adde vitest tests that show that this works when running with `env:
"BROWSERBASE"` and returns an empty string when `env: "LOCAL"`.

updates.summary_ru: Это изменение упрощает API потоковой передачи агентов путем перемещения флага `stream` из вызова API непосредственно в `AgentConfig`. Это обновление улучшает вывод типов TypeScript для метода `execute()`, позволяя ему корректно возвращать `AgentStreamResult` или `AgentResult` в зависимости от конфигурации. Рефакторинг также включает добавление поддержки потоковой передачи в `V3AgentHandler` и новый вспомогательный метод для общей логики настройки.
updates.source_content:
- Agents streaming (#1315)

# why

Simplify the agent streaming API by moving the `stream` flag into agent
configuration. This allows TypeScript to properly infer return types at
compile time and provides a cleaner API with a single `execute()`
method.

# what changed

- Added `stream?: boolean` to `AgentConfig`
- `agent({ stream: true }).execute()` → returns `AgentStreamResult`
- `agent().execute()` → returns `AgentResult` (unchanged)
- Added TypeScript overloads for proper type inference
- Added streaming support to `V3AgentHandler` and caching layer
- Extracted shared setup logic into `prepareAgentExecution()` helper

# test plan

- tested locally

- [vLLM][Core]: Add shutdown to vLLM connector (#1945)

* Add shutdown to vLLM connector

The vLLM connector does not shutdown LMCache gracefully. This
commit addsa shutdown method which calls cleanup methods for all
the objects that are created during the startup.

There are also updates to some of the cleanup methods of the objects
themselves to:

- Reduce deadlock and unsafe attribute access
- Add error handling and logging

Changes as follows:

1. `lmcache/integration/vllm/vllm_v1_adapter.py`
   - Added `shutdown()` method
   - Added timeout protection for all cleanup operations
   - Added missing resource cleanup
   - Added comprehensive logging
   - Added error tracking and reporting

2. `lmcache/v1/cache_engine.py`
   - Enhanced `close()` method with comprehensive logging
   - Enhanced `LMCacheEngineBuilder.destroy()` with detailed logging
   - Added error handling for all operations

3. `lmcache/v1/storage_backend/storage_manager.py`
   - Rewrote `close()` method with timeout protection
   - Added 10-second timeout to thread.join()
   - Added individual backend closure logging
   - Added error handling for event loop stop

4. `lmcache/v1/offload_server/zmq_server.py`
   - Enhanced `process_request()` with exception handling
   - Rewrote `close()` method with timeout
   - Added graceful thread termination
   - Added detailed logging

5. `lmcache/observability.py`
   - Rewrote `LMCacheStatsLogger.shutdown()` method with timeout protection
   - Added smart timeout calculation (log_interval + 2 seconds, minimum 5s)
   - Added comprehensive logging for stats logger shutdown
   - Added error handling for thread join

Основные изменения включают абстрагирование и унификацию парсинга, реализацию ленивой инициализации и валидации для сопоставления расширений файлов, а также исправление критической опечатки для правильного распознавания файлов `.cts` (модули TypeScript CommonJS). refactor(treeSitter): Abstract and unify tree-sitter parsing logic

- refactor(treeSitter): Clean up unused code and add defensive improvements

- Remove unused CommonCaptureTypes constant from BaseParseStrategy
  (each strategy uses its own CaptureType enum)
- Add readonly constraint to LANGUAGE_CONFIGS to prevent accidental mutation
- Add debug logging when guessTheLang encounters unsupported file extensions

Addresses minor code review suggestions for PR #967

- refactor(treeSitter): Add lazy initialization and extension collision validation

- Convert lookup map building to lazy initialization pattern to improve
  testability and avoid import-time side effects
- Add validation to detect duplicate extension claims between language configs,
  throwing an error if the same extension is claimed by multiple languages
- Address PR review comments from claude[bot] about module-level side effects
  and extension collision detection

- docs(treeSitter): Document intentional use of includes() in getCaptureTypes

Add JSDoc and inline comments explaining that includes() is used intentionally
to match hierarchical tree-sitter capture names (e.g., 'name.definition.function'
should match 'definition.function'). This is a design choice, not a bug.

- fix(treeSitter): Correct TypeScript extension typo 'ctx' to 'cts'

Fix typo inherited from original ext2Lang.ts where 'ctx' was incorrectly
used instead of 'cts' (TypeScript CommonJS module extension).

This ensures .cts files are properly recognized as TypeScript.

updates.source_content:
- fix(ci): test failures should fail the build (#3019)

The 'Check if tests exist' step was actually running tests with
continue-on-error: true. If tests failed, it would set has-tests=false
and skip the actual test step, making CI appear green even with failing tests.

Simplified to use 'npm test --if-present' which:
- Runs tests if a test script exists (and fails if tests fail)
- Does nothing and exits 0 if no test script exists
- Removes the need for the complex check logic

Fixes the issue where PR #3014 had failing tests but CI was green.

updates.summary_ru: Это обновление добавляет `ToolAnnotations` (подсказки о только для чтения, идемпотентности, деструктивности) ко всем инструментам файловой системы и документирует их в файле README. Это изменение решает проблему, когда клиенты рассматривали все операции файловой системы как универсальные операции записи. Теперь они могут точно различать действия только для чтения и записи, идентифицировать идемпотентные операции и выделять потенциально деструктивные. Данное улучшение обеспечивает более точную работу пользовательского интерфейса и логики повторных попыток, значительно повышая удобство для клиентов и пользователей.
updates.source_content:
- # feat(filesystem): add ToolAnnotations hints to filesystem tools (#3045)

**Files touched**

- [src/filesystem/index.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/filesystem/index.ts) — add `annotations` metadata to each tool definition
- [src/filesystem/README.md](../blob/HEAD/src/filesystem/README.md) — document ToolAnnotations mapping for all filesystem tools

## Description

This change adds MCP `ToolAnnotations` (`readOnlyHint`, `idempotentHint`, `destructiveHint`) to all filesystem tools and documents the mapping in the filesystem README. MCP clients can now accurately distinguish read‑only vs. write tools, understand which operations are safe to retry, and highlight potentially destructive actions.

## Server Details

- **Server**: filesystem
- **Area**: tools (metadata returned via `listTools` / `ListToolsRequest`) and server docs

## Motivation and Context

Previously, the filesystem server did not expose ToolAnnotations, so many clients (e.g. ChatGPT Apps) conservatively treated filesystem tools as generic write operations. This led to:

- READ operations being surfaced with WRITE badges and confirmation prompts.
- No way for clients to know which write tools are idempotent or potentially destructive.

This PR aligns the implementation with `servers#2988` and updates the README to clearly document the semantics of each tool. Read‑only operations no longer need to be treated as writes, and destructive/idempotent behavior is explicit for UI and retry logic.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `npm run build --workspace @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`
- `npm test --workspaces --if-present`

## Breaking Changes

None.

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

updates.title: Updates in main (16 commits)
updates.summary_ru:
This update significantly enhances the CTTI data synchronization process, introducing continuous sync with total limits, incremental updates, and more robust error handling for batch failures. It also improves tokenization and chunking logic by correctly handling special tokens in `tiktoken` and adding accurate token recounting to `CodeChunker`, preventing OpenAI API errors. Furthermore, critical fixes ensure user cache invalidation occurs reliably upon changes to organization membership, eliminating stale data issues and 403 errors.

***

Этот релиз значительно улучшает процесс синхронизации данных CTTI, внедряя непрерывную синхронизацию с общими лимитами, инкрементальные обновления и более надежную обработку ошибок при пакетных сбоях. Также улучшена логика токенизации и разделения на чанки за счет корректной обработки специальных токенов в `tiktoken` и добавления точного пересчета токенов в `CodeChunker`, что предотвращает ошибки OpenAI API. Кроме того, критические исправления гарантируют надежную инвалидацию пользовательского кеша при изменении членства в организации, устраняя проблемы устаревших данных и ошибки 403.
updates.source_content:
- Merge pull request #1144 from airweave-ai/feat/ctti-continuous-sync

Feat(CTTI): Continuous syncing with total limit

- fix(web_converter): don't fail entire sync on batch scrape failures

- Remove SyncFailureError when entire batch returns no results
- Return all None values instead, allowing entities to be skipped individually
- Only fail sync on true infrastructure errors (API key, auth, quota)
- Makes CTTI source more resilient to temporary unavailability
- Update docstrings to reflect new error handling behavior

- feat(ctti): implement continuous sync with total limit enforcement

- Add cursor_class=CTTICursor and supports_continuous=True
- Track last_nct_id for incremental sync (WHERE nct_id > cursor)
- Track total_synced to enforce configured limit across all sync runs
- Skip sync when limit is reached with clear log message
- Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
- Update docstrings to clarify limit is TOTAL, not per-sync

- feat(ctti): add CTTICursor schema for incremental sync

- Create CTTICursor with last_nct_id and total_synced fields
- NCT_IDs are strictly increasing, ideal for cursor-based pagination
- total_synced tracks records synced across all runs to enforce limit
- Export CTTICursor in cursors __init__.py

- Merge pull request #1143 from airweave-ai/fix/revamp_ctti

Fix: Create WebEntities that scrape urls

- Merge pull request #1141 from airweave-ai/fix/tiktoken-special-token-handling

Fix: handle special tokens in tiktoken encoding to prevent sync failures

- Merge pull request #1142 from airweave-ai/fix/user-cache-invalidation-on-org-creation

Fix: invalidate user cache when organization membership changes

- Merge branch 'fix/user-cache-invalidation-on-org-creation' into fix/revamp_ctti

- Merge branch 'fix/tiktoken-special-token-handling' into fix/revamp_ctti

- fix: invalidate user cache after transaction commit, not before

Address review feedback: invalidating the cache before the transaction
commits creates a race condition where another request could repopulate
the cache with stale data (the old user_organization rows are still
visible to other transactions until commit).

Changes:
- _delete_user_organization_relationships now returns the list of affected
  user emails instead of invalidating the cache directly
- delete_organization_with_auth0 invalidates caches after the commit
- remove_member_from_organization already had correct ordering (after commit)
- create_organization_with_integrations already had correct ordering (after commit)

- fix: invalidate user cache when organization membership changes

When a user creates a new organization, the cached user data (which includes
user_organizations) was not being invalidated. This caused 403 errors when
the user tried to access the new organization because the cached user data
still only contained their previous organizations.

This fix adds cache invalidation in three places:
1. After creating a new organization
2. After removing a member from an organization
3. When deleting an organization (for all affected users)

This ensures that whenever a user's organization membership changes, their
cached data is invalidated so the next API request will fetch fresh data
with the updated user_organizations list.

- fix: handle special tokens in tiktoken encoding to prevent sync failures

When user content contains special tokens like <|endoftext|> (e.g., from
AI-generated text pasted into Linear issues), tiktoken.encode() raises a
ValueError by default. This caused sync jobs to fail completely.

Fixed by passing allowed_special="all" to all tiktoken.encode() calls,
which treats special tokens as regular text for token counting purposes.
This is correct behavior since we're only counting tokens for chunk size
management, not constructing model inputs.

Affected files:
- semantic.py: _recount_tokens_with_tiktoken()
- code.py: _recount_tokens_with_tiktoken()
- entity_pipeline.py: chunk statistics logging
- openai.py: token counting in embedder
- _base.py: count_tokens() in search providers

Fixes Linear sync failures caused by special tokens in issue content.

- fix: accept failed status in schedule execution test

The test validates that a schedule triggers a sync job, not that the sync
succeeds. Jobs may fail due to rate limits from other tests running in the
same CI pipeline, which is outside the scope of this test.

- Merge pull request #1140 from airweave-ai/fix/code-chunker-token-limit

fix(chunker): Add tiktoken recount step to CodeChunker to fix token limit bypass

- fix(chunker): Add tiktoken recount step to CodeChunker to fix token limit bypass

Root cause: Chonkie's CodeChunker reports incorrect (understated) token counts
because it counts tokens from individual AST nodes only, but the final chunk
text includes whitespace/gaps between nodes plus leading/trailing content.

This caused chunks with 9760+ actual tokens to slip through the 8192-token
safety net (which checked the incorrect Chonkie count), resulting in OpenAI
embedding API errors in production.

Fix: Add Stage 1.5 (_recount_tokens_with_tiktoken) between AST chunking and
the safety net, identical to how SemanticChunker already handles this.
The safety net now uses accurate tiktoken counts and correctly triggers
TokenChunker fallback for oversized chunks.

Fixes token limit exceeded errors for GitHub code file syncs (HTML templates).

- fix(ctti): tune hyperparameters for larger chunks + increase concurrency embedding

updates.summary_ru: Функция `run` была рефакторизирована для значительного улучшения поддержки `stdin`/`stdout`, устраняя ряд проблем, возникших при разработке тестовых сценариев. Это обновление добавляет возможность передачи `Data` в `stdin`, исправляет блокировку каналов и облегчает прямое перенаправление двоичных данных из `stdout` в `stdin`. Данные изменения были реализованы в отдельном пулл-реквесте, чтобы не перегружать другие текущие работы.
updates.source_content:
- [tests]: refactor run function for stdin/stdout support (#830)

When working on test cases for #827 and #734 the following issues
occurred
  1. There was no support to pass in `Data` for `stdin` (input pipe added
    + new argument for the data)
  2. Pipes were getting blocked during the `try process.run()` and
    `process.waitUntilExit()` (order of operations were fixed)
  3. We need the binary data for directly piping the `stdout` data to
    `stdin`, and converting the data to a `string`, returns `""` (added a
    new value to the tuple)

I opened a new PR here for this as I did not want to bloat the other PRs
with so many updates. At first I thought of creating a new function
named `runStdinStdout`, but that seemed redundant as it pretty much was
going to do the same thing as `run`.

updates.title: Updates in main (5 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Основной новой функцией является команда CLI `container stats`, позволяющая пользователям отслеживать в реальном времени использование ЦП, памяти, сети, дискового ввода-вывода, а также количество процессов для одного или нескольких контейнеров. Безопасность была улучшена путем добавления проверки UID клиента на XPC-сервере для предотвращения несанкционированного доступа к контейнеру после выполнения команды `su`, а сборки контейнеров теперь поддерживают встроенные Dockerfile через стандартный ввод. Также было реализовано несколько исправлений ошибок, касающихся сборки статистики контейнеров, сбоев теста команды создания CLI и других внутренних сбоев тестов.
updates.source_content:
- Adds client uid validation to XPC server. (#896)

- When a user performs an `su` the effective UID changes but the bootstrap
  mach port does not, so that if container is running as `alice` from a
  GUI login session, it's possible to `su bob` and continue running
  container. While this doesn't pose a significant security risk as it's
  necessary for Alice to know Bob's password and manually enter it with
  `su`, this change closes the loophole by validating that client UID from
  the caller's audit token matches that of the API server.

- Fix container stats build break (#898)

Seems `run` was changed to return a data blob variant of stdout, which
made the function have a tuple of size 4 instead of 3 now. The stats
tests still used the old 3 wide variant which broke the build.

- Implement container stats (#851)

Closes #824

This implements statistics gathering across the various components, but
ultimately this is for implementing a new CLI command: `container
stats`. This shows memory usage, cpu usage, network and block i/o and
the number of processes in the container. The new command can inspect
stats for 1-N containers and by default continuously updates in a `top`
like stream.

Он также устраняет специфическую ошибку сборки Xcode, связанную с отсутствующим входным файлом (`CAuditToken.o`). Новая команда рассчитывает освобождаемое пространство из неактивных ресурсов и в будущем планируется к расширению с помощью дополнительных флагов.
updates.source_content:
- Build input file cannot be found: '.../CAuditToken.o' (#908)

Resolves a build error in Xcode:
> Build input file cannot be found: '.../CAuditToken.o'. Did you forget
to declare this file as an output of a script phase or custom build rule
which produces it?

- Add `container system df` command for disk usage reporting (#902)

- Closes #884. 

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature  
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update

## Motivation and Context
This PR implements the `container system df` command to display disk
usage statistics for images, containers, and volumes, along with their
total count, active count, size, and reclaimable space for each resource
type.

Active resources are determined by container mount references and
running state, while reclaimable space is calculated from inactive or
stopped resources.

Example output:
```
~/container ❯ container system df
TYPE           TOTAL  ACTIVE  SIZE      RECLAIMABLE
Images         4      3       4.42 GB   516.5 MB (11%)
Containers     4      2       2.69 GB   1.51 GB (56%)
Local Volumes  3      2       208.5 MB  66.2 MB (32%)
```

I'll have some follow-on PRs that will add `-v/--verbose` flag for
detailed per-resource information, `--filter` flag for filtering output
by resource type, and a `--debug` flag for debug statistics like block
usage, clone counts etc.

## Motivation and Context
Previously `container image prune` called `ImageStore.prune()` (renamed
to `cleanupOrphanedBlobs()` in cz 0.15.0) which only removed orphaned
content blobs and never actually removed images.

This PR fixes that behavior so `container image prune` removes dangling
images by default, and with `-a` removes all unused images, not just
dangling ones.

updates.summary_ru: В команду CLI transcribe добавлена новая функция, позволяющая выводить временные метки на уровне слов. Пользователи могут активировать ее с помощью флага `--word-timestamps`, который отображает точное время и оценки достоверности для каждого слова в расшифровке. Это улучшение упрощает анализ и синхронизацию расшифрованной речи с исходным аудио, обрабатывая и объединяя временные метки на уровне токенов из модели ASR.
updates.source_content:
- Add word-level timestamps support to CLI transcribe command (#193)

## Summary
fixes #189 
This PR adds a new `--word-timestamps` flag that displays timing
information for each word in the transcription output, making it easier
to analyze and synchronize transcribed speech with the original audio.

## Implementation Details

The feature works by:
1. Taking token-level timings from the ASR model output
2. Detecting word boundaries (whitespace characters)
3. Merging consecutive tokens into complete words
4. Averaging confidence scores across tokens that form each word

## Actual CLI Output

```
==================================================
[6:59:58.651 PM] [INFO] [FluidAudio.Transcribe] BATCH TRANSCRIPTION RESULTS
==================================================
[6:59:58.651 PM] [INFO] [FluidAudio.Transcribe] Final transcription:
Hello world!

Word-level timestamps:
  [0] 0.160s - 0.800s: "Hello" (conf: 0.999)
  [1] 0.800s - 1.440s: "world!" (conf: 0.771)

Performance:
  Audio duration: 1.48s
  Processing time: 0.12s
  RTFx: 12.07x
  Confidence: 0.862

[DEBUG] Token timings (count: 5):
  [0] ' H' (id: 425, start: 0.160s, end: 0.480s, conf: 0.998)
  [1] 'ello' (id: 3164, start: 0.480s, end: 0.800s, conf: 1.000)
  [2] ' wor' (id: 2088, start: 0.800s, end: 0.880s, conf: 0.953)
  [3] 'ld' (id: 2493, start: 0.880s, end: 1.360s, conf: 1.000)
  [4] '!' (id: 8020, start: 1.360s, end: 1.440s, conf: 0.362)
```


**Token merging example from output above:**
- ASR tokens: `[" H", "ello", " wor", "ld", "!"]` (5 tokens)
- Merged words: `["Hello", "world!"]` (2 words)
- **"Hello"**: Merged from `" H"` (0.160s-0.480s) + `"ello"`
(0.480s-0.800s) → 0.160s-0.800s
- **"world!"**: Merged from `" wor"` (0.800s-0.880s) + `"ld"`
(0.880s-1.360s) + `"!"` (1.360s-1.440s) → 0.800s-1.440s

Решение реализует защиту `#ifndef/#define`, чтобы гарантировать, что вызовы `cpp/raw` с одинаковым строковым содержимым считаются эквивалентными и выполняются только один раз.

Fixes #582 .

We use a simple #ifndef/#define guard, so all calls to `cpp/raw` that
have exactly the same content (same string) will be considered
equivalent and run only once.

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление значительно улучшает стабильность сборки и выполнения Jank на macOS, особенно в средах nix-darwin. Оно устраняет конфликты между стандартными библиотеками Clang, предоставляемыми ОС и локально собранными, а также улучшает AOT/JIT компиляцию за счет динамической обработки флагов компоновщика и фильтрации путей SDK для обеспечения переносимости. Кроме того, включены улучшения в синтаксический анализ ключевых слов и обработку ошибок.
updates.source_content:
- Clean up and document macOS stdinc fix (#603)

- Add clang args that fix the potential for OS and local Clang build std libs conflicting with each other. (#602)

* Add clang args that fix the potential for OS and local Clang build std libs conflicting with each other.

* Use the new flags conditionally on mac-like platforms.

- Make jank build portable on macOS in nix-darwin environments (#585)

This commit addresses build and runtime issues when jank is compiled on macOS
within a nix-darwin environment, making jank installable via Homebrew on macOS
even when nix-darwin is present.

## Problem

When building in nix-darwin, the SDKROOT and other environment variables are
set to point to nix-managed SDK paths. Although jank builds cleanly on vanilla
macOS, these nix-darwin settings interfere with the build process in two ways:

1. AOT Compilation: Platform-specific linker library requirements need proper
   handling. On macOS, Clang uses libc++ by default and doesn't require explicit
   -lstdc++ linking, while Linux requires it.

2. JIT Compilation: Clang extracts system include paths containing absolute SDK
   paths (e.g., /Applications/Xcode.app/.../MacOSX.sdk/usr/include or
   /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX*.sdk/usr/include). These
   paths get embedded in JANK_JIT_FLAGS and cause header ordering issues at
   runtime when jank performs JIT compilation.

## Solution

### Part 1: Platform-aware AOT compilation with runtime checks
- Moved -lstdc++ linking decision from build-time CMake to runtime C++ code
- Use if constexpr(jtl::current_platform != jtl::platform::macos_like) checks
- This approach is simpler and more maintainable than CMake configuration files
- On macOS: Exclude -lstdc++ (uses libc++ implicitly via Clang)
- On Linux: Include -lstdc++ (requires explicit linking)
- Removed -L/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/lib/unwind which is not needed on macOS

### Part 2: Filter SDK paths from JIT compilation flags
- Create a filtered version of clang_system_include_flags for JIT compilation
- Exclude paths matching /SDKs/ from JIT flags while preserving them for
  the build itself

This separation ensures:
- Build-time includes: Use unfiltered paths (need SDK headers for compilation)
- JIT runtime flags: Use filtered paths (SDK comes from -isysroot at JIT time)

The filtering prevents baking absolute SDK paths into the binary while still
allowing the build itself to find necessary system headers. At JIT time, the
correct SDK is obtained from -isysroot dynamically rather than hardcoded
build-time paths, making jank portable across different macOS/Nix configurations.

## Verification
- Builds successfully with SDKROOT set (nix-darwin environment)
- Builds successfully on vanilla macOS
- JIT compilation works correctly with filtered flags
- All check-health tests pass
- AOT compilation generates correct platform-specific binaries

- [DI] Support DI with DP

The main changes are tracking replica_idx in scheduler. When performing
a KVCache Transfer between Prefill -> Decode, we need to specify the
src and dst replica_idx. This should theoretically work even if the
Prefill
and Decode have different DP degrees.

This was tested with DP Llama on 4xH100 by running 4 seperate commands

- [TransferEngine] Support DP in transfer engine

Now the transfer engine supports both DP and TP.
This is needed for *D*P *D*eepseek with *D*I (The Triple-*D*).

The main difference now is that we specify the src and dst replica
indices
when we begin a transfer. Notice that the src and dst replicas can
differ.
```
// before
transfer_engine.initiate_send_transfer(
    remote_metadata=remote_metadata,
    src_idxs=src_idxs,
    dst_idxs=dst_idxs,
)

// after
transfer_engine.initiate_send_transfer(
    remote_metadata=remote_metadata,
    src_idxs=src_idxs,
    dst_idxs=dst_idxs,
    src_replica_idx=src_replica_idx,
    dst_replica_idx=dst_replica_idx,
)
```

Like how we already support TP, we use different NixlAgent per gpu for
DP.

There is no change needed at the NIXL layer. All the changes are purely
at
the Python transfer engine layer to support `list[list[Tensor]]` instead
of just `list[Tensor]`.

Although transfer engine supports DP + TP at same time, the rest of the
stack does not support them in combination yet fyi.

In a followup PR I will test that DP Llama works.
