- [DI] Simplify DI env vars and delete default destination address.

The env vars needed to configure DI are way too convoluted. I am
simplifying them here.

Sample old env var:
```
MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.207:7000", "default_destination_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000"}}'
```

This is annoying since it is a json string and we need to take care due
to double quotes and spaces.
You can easily mispecify this due to string escaping woes.

Additionally, it allows us to configure the transport type
("dynamic_zmq") when there are no other options.

Finally, it allows us to pass the "default_destination_address". This
refers to the default prefill node
to forward a request by a decode node if the target endpoint is not
specified for the request. This field
is meaningless for prefill nodes since they do not forward requests. I
am deleting this field and making it
a hard error if target endpoint is not specified for a request.

Now the new env var is much simpler:
```
MAX_SERVE_DI_BIND_ADDRESS=tcp://10.0.0.207:7000
```

This is a simple string that is easy to specify and read.

---

I am on privileged Gcore 2x8xH100 with Infiniband. This is two nodes
with 8 GPUs each.

Here is how to run deepseek with DI. We do not use multi-node EP here.

We use the `kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random` version since full
deepseek
does not fit on one 8xh100 node.

MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 is specified to
leave room
for nvshmem which allocates memory via cuMemCreate. If I set 99, I get a
crash
during inititalization.

prefill-chunk-size=128 is specified to minimize the amount of memory
that
nvshmem allocates.

---

Before:
```
// launch on decode node
MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 \
  MAX_SERVE_SCHEDULER_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_S=0 \
  UCX_TLS="rc,ud,dc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc" \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES="mlx5_ib0:1,mlx5_ib1:1,mlx5_ib2:1,mlx5_ib3:1,mlx5_ib4:1,mlx5_ib5:1,mlx5_ib6:1,mlx5_ib7:1" \
  MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.207:7000", "default_destination_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000"}}' \
  br //max -- serve --model-path=kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random \
  --pipeline-role=decode_only --devices=gpu:0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 --ep-size=8 --prefill-chunk-size=128

// launch on prefill node
MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 \
  MAX_SERVE_SCHEDULER_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_S=0 \
  UCX_TLS="rc,ud,dc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc" \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES="mlx5_ib0:1,mlx5_ib1:1,mlx5_ib2:1,mlx5_ib3:1,mlx5_ib4:1,mlx5_ib5:1,mlx5_ib6:1,mlx5_ib7:1" \
  MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000", "default_destination_address": "deadbeef"}}' \
```

- [MAX] Don't divide batch size by Data Parallelism degree

When you specify --data-parallel-degree 8 --max-batch-size 32 there are
two ways to interpret this:
1. Each of the 8 DP replicas has a cap on batch size of 32. Across all
replicas the aggregate max batch size is thus 8 * 32 = 256.
2. Each of the 8 DP replicas has a cap on batch size of 4. Across all
replicas the aggregate max batch size is thus 32.

Currently our code uses interpretation #2. However, I think we should
switch to #1 for the following reasons:
- Maintaining max_batch_size and max_batch_size_per_replica is very
error prone. It is very easy to mix them up.
- This interpretation is consistent to what vLLM does.

- [mojo-lang] Struct extensions naming/importing changes, attempt 2 (#72954)

Re-merges the compiler parts of
[Internal link] which were always fine
but caught up in the revert of the stdlib changes.

This PR does three main changes:

* Cleanup: Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) known to their
parents not as their struct's name ("MyStruct") but instead prefixed
with "extension:" ("extension:MyStruct"). This makes it so
lookupAndResolveDecl("MyStruct") doesn't return the extensions as well.
This is good because we generally like finding and resolving as little
as possible.
* Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) also known to their parents
as "extension:". This is helpful when we want to look up "all extensions
in a given scope", which is useful for the next point.
* Makes it so when we import anything from a module, we also import all
extensions (we just look for anything named "extension:").

Note that this might not be the final design, this makes an assumption
that if a file wants to use an extension, then that extension is in a
file that is indirectly imported. It's similar to Rust/Swift/C#/Kotlin,
but we might want to be more similar to Python, which just makes all
extensions globally visible to everyone everywhere, despite all the
spooky action at a distance that entails (doc incoming on this).

### [Kernels][FP4] Add NVFP4 dynamic scaled quantization kernel

This PR adds a quantization kernel for FP4 Activations. It follows the
same implementation as flashInfer and vLLM. For correctness check,
simillar to flashInfer we
use `rtol=atol=1e-1` for scalers and `rtol=1e0, atol=1e-1` for output
values. This is due to limitted accuracy of FP4 value. For example,
Float32(2.5) is mapped to FP4(2.0) and Float32(2.500001) is mapped to
3.0. Another approach for correctness check is to count number of errors
  and make sure they are less than a threshold.

Current limitations:

1. Only supports with NVFP4 (with minor changes it can also support
   MXFP4/MXFP8)
2. Only supports 2D (MxN) tensors for which `N % 8 == 0`.

MODULAR_ORIG_COMMIT_REV_ID: 6a2d8e9ea66ec1fa15ce024a8eefd5ef8d34a987

- [mojo-lang] Struct extensions naming/importing changes (#72612)

Re-merges the compiler parts of
[Internal link] which were always fine
but caught up in the revert of the stdlib changes.

This PR does three main changes:

* Cleanup: Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) known to their
parents not as their struct's name ("MyStruct") but instead prefixed
with "extension:" ("extension:MyStruct"). This makes it so
lookupAndResolveDecl("MyStruct") doesn't return the extensions as well.
This is good because we generally like finding and resolving as little
as possible.
* Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) also known to their parents
as "extension:". This is helpful when we want to look up "all extensions
in a given scope", which is useful for the next point.
* Makes it so when we import anything from a module, we also import all
extensions (we just look for anything named "extension:").

Note that this might not be the final design, this makes an assumption
that if a file wants to use an extension, then that extension is in a
file that is indirectly imported. It's similar to Rust/Swift/C#/Kotlin,
but we might want to be more similar to Python, which just makes all
extensions globally visible to everyone everywhere, despite all the
spooky action at a distance that entails (doc incoming on this).

- [max] Reduce number of unused layers during DeepSeek R1 construction (#72811)

The constructors for many layer types (e.g. Linear, MoE, MLP) initialize
their child layer during construction. When sharding, the child layers
are discarded in favor of the sharded versions of those layers.

This results in a large amount of time spent constructing various layer
instances that are never used (small millions of layers).

This change reworks the constructors for Linear, MoE, and MLP layers to
not build their child layers during the sharding process. This drops the
graph build time from ~27 seconds to ~14 seconds.

- [stdlib] Simplify SIMD dunder relational methods

This commit simplifies several SIMD dunder relational methods.

The methods work by calling into their respective non-dunder variants,
which return SIMD bool vectors. Those are then used to create a `Bool`
using the constructor and the `ImplicitlyBoolable` trait, which calls
back into SIMD's `__bool__` method.

Instead, we can avoid this roundtrip by calling `__bool__` ourselves.
This keeps things in the SIMD domain and avoids the trait interface.

An added benefit of this is that this specific `Bool` constructor is not
supported by `@always_inline("builtin")` due to an unsupported argument
convention. Future work will thus be able to mark these dunder
relational methods `@always_inline("builtin")` and enable better support
for SIMD types in `where` clauses.

updates.title: Updates in main (7 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Версия 0.5.5 включает значительные улучшения пользовательского интерфейса и опыта (UI/UX) в таких функциях, как регистрация, список команд, поисковое окно, запуск рабочих процессов и индикатор использования. Также были проведены ключевые технические миграции на ReactQuery и Tanstack для повышения производительности и улучшения управления хранилищами данных. Кроме того, обновление расширяет возможности работы с переменными, добавляя поддержку точечной нотации для вложенных объектов, и устраняет ряд проблем, связанных с переменными, папками и блоками ответов.

updates.summary_ru: Введено необязательный параметр `verify` для `MCPClient` и его коннекторов, позволяющий контролировать проверку SSL-сертификатов и обеспечивающий единообразную обработку SSL. Также менеджеры соединений SSE и Streamable HTTP теперь поддерживают пользовательские фабрики клиентов HTTPX, что повышает гибкость в управлении соединениями.
updates.source_content:
- feat: Add verify parameter to MCPClient and connectors (#478)

* feat: add verify parameter to MCPClient and connectors

- Introduced a new optional `verify` parameter in `MCPClient`, `HttpConnector`, and configuration functions to control SSL certificate verification.
- Updated relevant methods to utilize the `verify` parameter, ensuring consistent handling of SSL verification across the client and connectors.
- Enhanced the SSE and Streamable HTTP connection managers to accept a custom HTTPX client factory for improved flexibility in connection handling.

updates.summary_ru: Обновление вносит значительные улучшения в клиент Python, включая интеграцию «режима кода», новый параметр `verify` для обработки SSL-сертификатов и улучшенное «красивое» отображение вывода. Инструменты разработчика усилены инспектором с логированием консоли iframe, улучшенной функцией туннелирования с поддержкой поддоменов и расширенным управлением режимами отображения для виджетов. Пользовательский опыт улучшен за счет управления серверными соединениями, динамической загрузки и кэширования моделей ИИ от различных провайдеров, а также более удобной обработки аргументов инструментов. Была также значительно обновлена документация по туннелированию, инспектору и серверу TypeScript.

(#11536) ### What problem does this PR solve? ##### Problem Description When parsing HTML files, some page content may be lost. For example, text inside nested `` tags within multiple `
` elements (e.g., `
Text_1
Text_2
`) fails to be preserved correctly. ###### Root Cause #1: Block ID propagation is interrupted 1. **Block ID generation**: When the parser encounters a `
`, it generates a new `block_id` because `
` belongs to `BLOCK_TAGS`. 2. **Recursive processing**: This `block_id` is passed down recursively to process the `
`’s child nodes. 3. **Interruption occurs**: When processing a child `` tag, the code enters the `else` branch of `read_text_recursively` (since `` is a Tag). 4. **Bug location**: The first line in this `else` branch explicitly sets **`block_id = None`**. - This discards the valid `block_id` inherited from the parent `
`. - Since `` is not in `BLOCK_TAGS`, it does not generate a new `block_id`, so it passes `None` to its child text nodes. 5. **Consequence**: The extracted text nodes have an empty `block_id` in their `metadata`. During the subsequent `merge_block_text` step, these texts cannot be correctly associated with their original `
` block due to the missing ID. As a result, all text from `` tags gets merged together, which then triggers a second issue during concatenation. 6. **Solution:** Remove the forced reset of `block_id` to `None`. When the current tag (e.g., ``) is not a block-level element, it should inherit the `block_id` passed down from its parent. This ensures consistent ownership across the hierarchy: `div` → `font` → `text`. ###### Root Cause #2: Data loss during text concatenation 1. The line `current_content += (" " if current_content else "" + content)` has a misplaced parenthesis. When `current_content` is non-empty (`True`): - The ternary expression evaluates to `" "` (a single space). - The code executes `current_content += " "`. - **Result**: Only a space is appended—**the new `content` string is completely discarded**. ### Type of change - [x] Bug Fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- Export progress updates (#437)

The goal of these changes is to export allocation progress updates
generated inside FE in order to expose them from an SSE api. The
`update` function in `RequestCtx` should also allow users to add
additional information like a message, or extra attributes that clients
can consume later to present detailed information about the progress
update.

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Данное обновление интегрирует API Google Gemini 3 в конвейер оптического распознавания символов (OCR). Оно также включает значительный рефакторинг удаленного APIClient, направленный на улучшение читаемости кода, стандартизацию обработки ошибок (с генерированием только исключений, производных от TensorlakeError), обеспечение единообразной политики повторных попыток и предоставление более понятных сообщений об ошибках. Помимо этого, были рефакторингированы тесты контекста запросов, фронтенд теперь обрабатывает операции чтения/записи больших двоичных объектов (BLOB), а также исправлена ошибка в его логгере.
updates.source_content:
- feat: google gemini in ocr pipeline provider (#454)

## Descriptioin

- The addition of Google Gemini 3 API in OCR Models.

- Refactor and fix remote APIClient (#451)

The current remote APIClient code was derived from a fairly old SDK code
base. Because of this remote APIClient has both stylistic issues and
coding bugs now.

This PR does the following:

* Add type hints everywhere to make it easier to read code.
* Don't user variadic args and kwargs as it makes reading code harder.
* Only raise exceptions derived from TensorlakeError. We were raising
arbitrary unexpected exception types directly into user code while all
SDK code should raise exceptions derived from TensorlakeError.
* Use consistent retry policy in sse stream and regular http requests.
* Remove unused pydantic model definitions for Server API. We'll add the
models back if we need them in future projects. Having them in remote
APIClient requires us keeping them updated which might slow down some
future work. This is also effectively a dead code.
* Define code structure in remote APIClient that other people can follow
in the future and not introduce hard to notice mistakes because it's
Python.
* Give more descriptive user friendly error messages in certain cases
like no auth credentials present on HTTP 401 code.
* Don't use httpx client event hooks because they make the APIClient
error handling behavior hard to reason about i.e. it makes exceptions
raised by ApiClient dependant on how it was created. The existing hooks
raise ClickException which has nothing to do with TensorlakeError which
is a base class for all errors in SDK components which include
APIClient.

Testing:

* Checked all callers of APIClient methods to make sure that none of
them break if we start only raising TensorlakeError derived exceptions.
* Manually ran all tensorlake CLI commands.
* All integration tests pass.

- Refactor request context tests (#453)

Move them to a dedicated directory and add missing basic tests for
existing API.

- Move request state read/writes into FE (#448)

The BLOBs (presigned URLs) for reading/writing are supplied by Executor.
Actual read/writes are done on FE side.

Also fix FE logger bug introduced after we started to use Cloud Events
to print FE logs. The FE logger started to fail logging if a log tag is
not json serializable. FE logger must be absolutely reliable and not
raise exceptions itself.

All tests pass locally with Indexify PR
https://github.com/tensorlakeai/indexify/pull/1892

updates.source_content:
- feat(tools): Add debug logging to VertexAiSearchTool

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/3284

**Problem:**
When debugging agents that utilize the `VertexAiSearchTool`, it's currently difficult to inspect the specific configuration parameters (datastore ID, engine ID, filter, max_results, etc.) being passed to the underlying Vertex AI Search API via the `LlmRequest`. This lack of visibility can hinder troubleshooting efforts related to tool configuration.

**Solution:**
This PR enhances the `VertexAiSearchTool` by adding a **debug-level log statement** within the `process_llm_request` method. This log precisely records the parameters being used for the Vertex AI Search configuration just before it's appended to the `LlmRequest`.

This provides developers with crucial visibility into the tool's runtime behavior when debug logging is enabled, significantly improving the **debuggability** of agents using this tool. Corresponding unit tests were updated to rigorously verify this new logging output using `caplog`. Additionally, minor fixes were made to the tests to resolve Pydantic validation errors.

Co-authored-by: Xuan Yang <xygoogle@google.com>

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление в основном представляет миграцию DatabaseSessionService на схему сериализации JSON, а также новый инструмент командной строки `adk migrate session` для миграции базы данных. Также добавлен APIRegistryToolset для интеграции инструментов из реестра Cloud API в агенты и улучшена прогрессивная потоковая передача SSE для поддержки потоковой передачи аргументов вызовов функций. Наконец, исправление устраняет проблему с параметром `per_agent` при использовании URI удаленных сеансовых сервисов.
updates.source_content:
- feat!: Migrate DatabaseSessionService to use JSON serialization schema

Also provide a command line tool `adk migrate session` for DB migration

Addresses https://github.com/google/adk-python/discussions/3605
Addresses https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/3681

To verify:
```
# Start one postgres DB
docker run --name my-postgres -d -e POSTGRES_DB=agent  -e POSTGRES_USER=agent  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=agent  -e PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata -v pgvolume:/var/lib/postgresql/data -p 5532:5432 postgres

# Connect to an old version of ADK and produce some query data
adk web --session_service_uri=postgresql://agent:agent@localhost:5532/agent

# Check out to the latest branch and restart ADK web
# You should see error log ask you to migrate the DB

# Start a new DB
docker run --name migration-test-db \
  -d \ --rm \ -e POSTGRES_DB=agent \ -e POSTGRES_USER=agent \ -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=agent -e PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata -v migration_test_vol:/var/lib/postgresql/data -p 5533:5432 postgres

# DB Migration
adk migrate session \
  --source_db_url="postgresql://agent:agent@localhost:5532/agent" \
  --dest_db_url="postgresql://agent:agent@localhost:5533/agent"

# Run ADK web with the new DB
adk web --session_service_uri=postgresql+asyncpg://agent:agent@localhost:5533/agent

# You should see the data from old DB is migrated
```

Co-authored-by: Shangjie Chen <deanchen@google.com>
PiperOrigin-RevId: 837341139

Co-authored-by: Xuan Yang <xygoogle@google.com>

Co-authored-by: George Weale <gweale@google.com>
PiperOrigin-RevId: 837169299

- feat: Create APIRegistryToolset to add tools from Cloud API registry to agent

This calls the cloudapiregistry.googleapis.com API to get MCP tools from the project's registry, and adds them to ADK.

updates.source_content:
- `StreamlitMarkdown` - module level plugin cache (#13152)

React's `StrictMode` exposed some opportunities to improve the recently added lazy loading for `StreamlitMarkdown`'s plugins:`rehype-katex`,`rehype-raw`, & `remark-emoji`

Component is now StrictMode compatible, with improved performance (plugins load once per app, not per component instance), and better handle plugin load failure (render as plain text).

This PR better makes the following changes:
* **Module-level caching**: Moved plugin storage outside React's
component lifecycle to share across instances and persist across
re-renders
* **Adds custom `useLazyPlugin` hook**: Consolidated three
nearly-identical useEffect blocks into a single reusable hook with
proper cleanup handling
* **Extraction to `utils.ts`**: Moved all plugin-related logic (types,
loaders, cache, helpers, hook) to a dedicated file

- Improve `st.line_chart` hovering performance (#13156)

## Describe your changes

Improves the hovering performance of `st.line_chart` with larger
datasets.
